<file name="SCHEMA.sql" language="plaintext" >
<content>
ALTER TABLE "ApprovalAudit" ADD PRIMARY KEY ("tenantId","purchaseId","approvedBy",operation,"idempotencyKey");
CREATE TABLE "PurchaseEvent" (
  "tenantId" text NOT NULL,
  "purchaseId" text NOT NULL,
  type text NOT NULL,
  "actorId" text NOT NULL,
  "idempotencyKey" text NOT NULL,
  "createdAt" timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  "deliveredAt" timestamptz,
  PRIMARY KEY ("tenantId","purchaseId",type,"actorId","idempotencyKey"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("tenantId","purchaseId") REFERENCES "Purchase" ("tenantId",id)
);
ALTER TABLE "PurchaseEvent" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE "PurchaseEvent" FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
REVOKE ALL ON "PurchaseEvent" FROM app_runtime;
GRANT SELECT,INSERT ON "PurchaseEvent" TO app_runtime;
CREATE POLICY purchase_event_read ON "PurchaseEvent" FOR SELECT TO app_runtime USING
 ("tenantId"=current_setting('app.tenant',true) AND current_setting('app.role',true) IN ('approver','requester'));
CREATE POLICY purchase_event_insert ON "PurchaseEvent" FOR INSERT TO app_runtime WITH CHECK
 ("tenantId"=current_setting('app.tenant',true) AND "actorId"=current_setting('app.user',true) AND current_setting('app.role',true) IN ('approver','requester'));
DROP POLICY action_request_read ON "ActionRequest";
DROP POLICY action_request_insert ON "ActionRequest";
CREATE POLICY action_request_read ON "ActionRequest" FOR SELECT TO app_runtime USING
 ("tenantId"=current_setting('app.tenant',true) AND "actorId"=current_setting('app.user',true) AND current_setting('app.role',true) IN ('approver','requester'));
CREATE POLICY action_request_insert ON "ActionRequest" FOR INSERT TO app_runtime WITH CHECK
 ("tenantId"=current_setting('app.tenant',true) AND "actorId"=current_setting('app.user',true) AND current_setting('app.role',true) IN ('approver','requester'));
DROP POLICY approval_audit_insert ON "ApprovalAudit";
CREATE POLICY approval_audit_insert ON "ApprovalAudit" FOR INSERT TO app_runtime WITH CHECK
 ("tenantId"=current_setting('app.tenant',true) AND "approvedBy"=current_setting('app.user',true) AND current_setting('app.role',true) IN ('approver','requester'));
-- Replaces the v4 decide policy (the guarded runtime requires exactly three Purchase policies).
DROP POLICY purchase_decide ON "Purchase";
CREATE POLICY purchase_transition ON "Purchase" FOR UPDATE TO app_runtime
 USING ("tenantId" = current_setting('app.tenant', true) AND (
   (current_setting('app.role', true) = 'approver' AND "createdBy" <> current_setting('app.user', true) AND status = 'submitted')
   OR (current_setting('app.role', true) = 'requester' AND "createdBy" = current_setting('app.user', true) AND status = 'rejected')))
 WITH CHECK ("tenantId" = current_setting('app.tenant', true) AND (
   (current_setting('app.role', true) = 'approver' AND status IN ('approved','rejected'))
   OR (current_setting('app.role', true) = 'requester' AND "createdBy" = current_setting('app.user', true) AND status = 'submitted')));

-- v6b additive disposable POC schema, applied after the v3 Action, v4 reject and v5 reopen schemas.
-- Tenant members, and an assignee per purchase that approvers may change while it is submitted.
CREATE TABLE "TenantMember" (
  "tenantId" text NOT NULL,
  "userId" text NOT NULL,
  role text NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('approver','requester')),
  active boolean NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("tenantId","userId")
);
ALTER TABLE "TenantMember" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE "TenantMember" FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
REVOKE ALL ON "TenantMember" FROM app_runtime;
GRANT SELECT ON "TenantMember" TO app_runtime;
CREATE POLICY tenant_member_read ON "TenantMember" FOR SELECT TO app_runtime USING
 ("tenantId"=current_setting('app.tenant',true) AND current_setting('app.role',true) IN ('approver','requester'));
INSERT INTO "TenantMember" ("tenantId","userId",role,active) VALUES
 ('tenant-a','alice','requester',true),('tenant-a','bob','approver',true),('tenant-a','carol','approver',true),
 ('tenant-a','hana','approver',true),('tenant-a','frank','approver',false),
 ('tenant-b','dave','requester',true),('tenant-b','erin','approver',true),('tenant-b','ivan','approver',true);
ALTER TABLE "Purchase" ADD COLUMN "assigneeId" text;
ALTER TABLE "Purchase" ADD FOREIGN KEY ("tenantId","assigneeId") REFERENCES "TenantMember" ("tenantId","userId");
GRANT SELECT ("assigneeId") ON "Purchase" TO app_runtime;
GRANT UPDATE ("assigneeId") ON "Purchase" TO app_runtime;
CREATE TABLE "AssignmentHistory" (
  "tenantId" text NOT NULL,
  "purchaseId" text NOT NULL,
  "fromAssignee" text,
  "toAssignee" text NOT NULL,
  "changedBy" text NOT NULL,
  operation text NOT NULL,
  "idempotencyKey" text NOT NULL,
  "createdAt" timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
  PRIMARY KEY ("tenantId","purchaseId","changedBy",operation,"idempotencyKey"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("tenantId","purchaseId") REFERENCES "Purchase" ("tenantId",id)
);
ALTER TABLE "AssignmentHistory" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE "AssignmentHistory" FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
REVOKE ALL ON "AssignmentHistory" FROM app_runtime;
GRANT SELECT,INSERT ON "AssignmentHistory" TO app_runtime;
CREATE POLICY assignment_history_read ON "AssignmentHistory" FOR SELECT TO app_runtime USING
 ("tenantId"=current_setting('app.tenant',true) AND current_setting('app.role',true) IN ('approver','requester'));
CREATE POLICY assignment_history_insert ON "AssignmentHistory" FOR INSERT TO app_runtime WITH CHECK
 ("tenantId"=current_setting('app.tenant',true) AND "changedBy"=current_setting('app.user',true) AND current_setting('app.role',true)='approver');
ALTER TABLE "ActionRequest" DROP CONSTRAINT "ActionRequest_operation_check";
ALTER TABLE "ActionRequest" ADD CONSTRAINT "ActionRequest_operation_check" CHECK (operation IN ('bulk-approve.v3','bulk-reject.v4','reopen.v5','bulk-reassign.v6'));
-- Replaces the v5 transition policy (the guarded runtime requires exactly three Purchase policies):
-- an approver may also keep a submitted purchase submitted while changing its assignee.
DROP POLICY purchase_transition ON "Purchase";
CREATE POLICY purchase_transition ON "Purchase" FOR UPDATE TO app_runtime
 USING ("tenantId" = current_setting('app.tenant', true) AND (
   (current_setting('app.role', true) = 'approver' AND "createdBy" <> current_setting('app.user', true) AND status = 'submitted')
   OR (current_setting('app.role', true) = 'requester' AND "createdBy" = current_setting('app.user', true) AND status = 'rejected')))
 WITH CHECK ("tenantId" = current_setting('app.tenant', true) AND (
   (current_setting('app.role', true) = 'approver' AND status IN ('approved','rejected','submitted'))
   OR (current_setting('app.role', true) = 'requester' AND "createdBy" = current_setting('app.user', true) AND status = 'submitted')));

</content>
</file>

I added `POST /purchases/bulk-reassign`. It builds and passes `go vet`, but it has never run against a database. The database credentials weren't available and the repo has no test files, so `go test ./...` checked nothing.

**What changed (only in `internal/candidate/`):**
- `operations.go`: a new `reassignOp` is declared as an `action.Update`. It is named `bulk-reassign.v6`, needs the `approver` role, targets purchases created by other users, requires status `submitted`, sets the `assigneeId` column and returns the IDs under `reassignedIds`.
- `approval.go`: a handler calls `executor.Set` and turns kernel rejections into `protocol.Rejection` through the existing `adapt` function. The route is registered with `protocol.Assign("/purchases/bulk-reassign", ...)` between the batch routes and the `reopen` route, so bulk-approve, bulk-reject and reopen behave as before.

**How the requirements are covered:**
- **Input and identity:** `protocol.Assign` checks the request body, the authenticated identity (401 or 403), the body size limit and the Idempotency-Key.
- **Kernel checks:** `Set` checks that the assignee is an active approver in the tenant's `TenantMember` table and that every target is someone else's `submitted` purchase. Any failure returns 409 and the whole batch rolls back.
- **Idempotency:** the request fingerprint covers both the operation name with the assignee and the ID list. A replay of the same request returns the stored IDs with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. The same key with different IDs or a different assignee returns 409.
- **Same transaction:** the `ActionRequest` row is written in the same transaction as the change. If that write fails, the error falls through to 503 and nothing is saved.
- **Replay bytes:** the response is encoded as `{"assignee":...,"reassignedIds":[...]}`. Go sorts map keys when encoding, so a replay produces the same bytes as the first response.

**Your decision:** I set `Event: action.NoEvent` because the spec doesn't mention an outbox event, so no `PurchaseEvent` row is written. Each reassignment still adds one `AssignmentHistory` row per target. The kernel does this itself and it can't be turned off.
